text: In 1974, five residents of Strongsville, OH, sued the board of education to remove Ken Kesey's One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest, calling it "pornographic" and charging that it "glorifies criminal activity, has a tendency to corrupt juveniles and contains descriptions of bestiality, bizarre violence, and torture, dismemberment, death, and human elimination." In 1975 the novel was removed from public school libraries in Randolph, NY, and Alton, OK. In 1978 it was banned from the St. Anthony, ID Freemont High School classrooms and the instructor was fired; the teacher sued, but the decision in the case, Fogarty v. Atchley, was never published. It was challenged at the Merrimack, NH High School in 1982. In 1986 it was challenged in an Aberdeen, WA High School honors English class because it promotes "secular humanism," and the school board voted to retain it.
meta_description: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest by Ken Kesey: sued over in Strongsville, OH, in 1974, removed in 1975, banned from classrooms in 1978, kept in Aberdeen, WA, in 1986.
changes: Events in date order; 1975 removals combined; case name and quoted charges taken from the source quotes.
